newsitem.title: UK: Metals Outlook - Copper stocks remain in spotlight.
newsitem.headline: Metals Outlook - Copper stocks remain in spotlight.

text.p: The industrial metals market will keep a sharp eye on copper inventories this week after it sailed through $2,000 per tonne on the London Metal Exchange (LME) only to sink in late dealings on Friday.
Aluminium and its tight January dates will also remain in the spotlight.

And a meeting this week between LME Chief Executive David King and the UK regulatory Securities and Investment Board (SIB) will be closely watched. The SIB has been reviewing the metals trade in the aftermath of the Sumitomo copper scandal.
On the markets, flagship copper started last week calmly, locked in a tight range even though LME inventories, already at the lowest for six years, eroded further.
Stocks fell by 10,300 tonnes over the week, to 113,400 tonnes, down by over 50 percent over the past two months.
But players are wary that not all the metal moving out of exchange warehouses may be going to consumption but may show up in Singapore inventories.
Prices soared on Thursday as investment funds and short-covering pushed prices up $42, breaching the psychological $2,000 level.
The market had difficulty, however, making further progress as profit-taking and producer selling dented attempts to challenge next levels of resistance at $2,020 and $2,040/50.
It slid below $2,000 in this, late inter-office activity on Friday night.
Aluminium eased with it from a week's high at $1,468 but also knocked over some upside barriers as it gained some $30 over the week and traded late on Friday around $1,450 per tonne.

The market was boosted by a narrowing contango as tightness developed in January dates when short players scurried to cover positions and found the near one million tonnes of LME stocks were not readily available.
The gains in copper and aluminium had inspired one analyst to predict a turnaround in the base metals bear market.
"Every one of the main and intermediate metal price booms since the 1970s has begun in the month of November," said Nick Moore of Flemings Global Mining Group.
"This month will be the turning point in the cycle, opening a fresh and far more positive chapter for 1997 which will culminate in the end-cycle commodity boom in the fourth quarter 1997," he added.
The LME chief King said at a conference in Australia last Wednesday that he would meet with the SIB this week to focus on the outcome of a review by the watchdog of exchange users.
The discussions would include how the LME provided price transparency, operated its warehousing system and other issues. --London Newsroom +44 171 542 8065
